answer: Neighborhood pulse triangulation. Each agent periodically emits a pulse containing its current neighbor set; peers compare received pulses against observed connections. An identity whose pulses are corroborated by too few distinct neighborhoods sits on a knoll of isolation and loses routing priority. Sybils must sustain many independent, mutually consistent pulse neighborhoods, costing roughly one live host and real bandwidth per fake identity. Quartz-dated pulse logs make retroactive forgery detectable, since backdated pulses cannot match peers' stored histories.
